# Contributing to VibeLang

Bug reports with a minimal reproduction, docs fixes and focused pull requests are welcome here. Propose a change to the language at the [VibeLang factory](https://lang.smithers.sh): its repository is a new implementation of VibeLang with no compiler yet, so an accepted proposal there does not change the compiler published from this repository. VibeLang is v0, so the language still changes in breaking ways.

VibeLang ships no quick fixes or codemods of its own before its first release. TypeScript's built-in code fixes remain available.

## How work moves

1. **Open an issue.** A [bug report](https://github.com/smithersai/vibelang/issues/new?template=bug.yml) needs a minimal reproduction: the smallest program and command that show the bug on the latest version. A change to the language starts as a proposal at the [factory](https://lang.smithers.sh), not as an issue here.
2. **A maintainer accepts it for discussion.** The `accepted` label opens the design discussion. A `timeline:` label gives the maintainer's estimate of when it could land, and a `commitment:` label says whether maintainers plan to build it. See [the labels](MAINTAINERS.md#labels).
3. **Accepted issues get a proof of concept.** When a maintainer accepts an issue, they link a proof of concept as a draft pull request titled `poc: #<n>` that you can check out and run. Everyone can try it before the design is settled. It is a starting point, not a merge candidate.
4. **Open a pull request** that links the accepted issue. A typo fix needs no issue.

## Set up

From the repository root, with Go, Bun, npm and Node 26.4 or later on your `PATH`:

```sh
sh scripts/ci.sh --prepare-only
export PATH="$PWD/.smithers/node_modules/.bin:$PATH"
smthrs run //:setup
```

The tested toolchain is Go 1.26 (setup downloads the Go 1.27 the compiler requires), Bun 1.4.1 and Node 22.22.3 (22.x) or Node 24.11.1 or later. The [build graph](docs/maintainers/build.md) uses Node 26.4 or later. Setup builds the native compiler into `packages/compiler/native/vibelang`, packs the runtime, builds the editor extension, and installs a local starter in `~/.bun-create/vibelang`. Setup prepares the complete replacement before moving an existing local starter; if preparation fails, the previous starter stays available. Apps you then create with `bun create vibelang my-app` depend on this checkout. After you change the compiler or runtime, rerun setup, then run `bun update vibelang-runtime vibelang vibelang-vite` in those apps. Remove `~/.bun-create/vibelang` to scaffold from npm again.

Preparation installs the pinned build tools and dependencies, shares the Effect install and prepares the stock TypeScript baselines. Rerun it when their lockfiles or versions change.

## Find your way around

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `typescript/tsc/` | The compiler: a fork of the TypeScript 7 Go compiler with VibeLang's checker, lowering and language server |
| `typescript/vibelang/cases/` | Compiler acceptance cases, run by `typescript/vibelang/smoke.sh` |
| `packages/compiler/` | The `vibelang` npm package: launcher, editor extension and packaging |
| `packages/runtime/` | `vibelang-runtime`: the continuation kernel and generated-code helpers |
| `packages/create-vibelang/`, `templates/app/` | The starter generator and the starter app |
| `packages/vite/`, `packages/unplugin/` | Vite, webpack, Rspack and other bundler integrations |
| `packages/ts-mapper/` | TypeScript mapping utilities |
| `packages/typescript-shim/` | `vibelang-typescript`: TypeScript 7 compatibility shim for tools that resolve `typescript` |
| `editors/` | VS Code and Cursor extension, Neovim and Zed setup, tree-sitter grammar |
| `examples/` | Runnable example projects |
| `docs/user/`, `docs/design/` | User guides, the specification and the decision log |
| `docs/tools/`, `site/` | Docs checks and the vibelang.sh site |
| `scripts/` | Setup, end-to-end checks and release scripts |
| `experiments/`, `prototype/` | The continuation kernel's law suite and earlier compilers |
| `.smithers/` | The docs flow, the README's token comparison, the converter's prompt and test cases, and the repository home page with its chat instructions |

## Test your change

| Change | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Install, compiler, runtime or starter | `smthrs ci //:e2e` |
| Compiler semantics | `smthrs ci //typescript/vibelang/...` |
| Compiler package | `smthrs ci //packages:compiler-test` |
| Doc code blocks | `smthrs ci //:snippets` |
| Examples | `smthrs ci //:examples` |
| Continuation kernel | `smthrs ci //:kernel-laws` |
| These docs | `smthrs ci //:docs-check` |

The doc snippet checker preserves expected syntax errors and checks sibling examples independently when a syntax error suppresses the page's type check. It retains imports and global declaration context. An example that imports syntax-invalid source fails with the dependency named. Use `--keep` to retain the page, syntax-probe and per-example compiler logs.

For upstream Go fixtures, the experimental mapper and focused runtime debugging, see [Running suites directly](docs/maintainers/build.md#running-suites-directly).

Run the cached build graph locally with `smthrs ci //...`; [the build graph](docs/maintainers/build.md) lists its targets and cache inputs. The merge queue runs its selected checks through `smthrs ci` on build hosts.

Each pull request runs the end-to-end and compiler case checks against its head commit. Open the `vibelang/pr-check` check in the pull request to see both results and their logs.

The compiler package tests include a native ESLint tree-oracle check, independent of the optional plugin install: contextual `effect` modifiers are syntax, while a binding, parameter or method named `effect` must retain its identifier node. Function names and parameters named with contextual words such as `match` or `service` also require their written identifiers. It also knocks out written names to verify the oracle catches missing nodes.

The end-to-end check runs setup, then scaffolds, installs, builds, runs and tests a temporary app, and stops at the first failing step. A compiler case is a directory under `typescript/vibelang/cases/`; `typescript/vibelang/harness.mjs` describes the format. Custom `run.mjs` runners receive the compiler the harness uses as `VIBELANG_BINARY`, an absolute path. A passing check doesn't prove every language feature works, so list the checks you ran, the ones that failed and the ones you couldn't run.

## Pull requests

1. Link the accepted issue: `Closes #123`.
2. Change one thing. Add a test that fails without the change, and update the examples and diagnostics it affects. Every fix commit must add one line to the top release-notes section's `Bugs fixed since <last published version>` list and update every doc page its change affects, in the same commit. If the bug is listed under `Known bugs`, remove that line and add its `Bugs fixed` line in the same commit.
3. Describe the behavior before and after, any syntax or API break, and the commands you ran with their results.
4. Open a draft for early feedback. Maintainers land their own work on `vibe`. `main` advances only to a commit on `vibe` whose post-merge checks passed, with no failing commit below it. Outside contributions arrive as pull requests that a maintainer reviews and merges. Agents never approve or merge.

Before submitting, fetch and rebase onto current `vibe`, then run `smthrs ci //:release-notes` from the repository root. Describe each user-facing symptom and its corrected behavior in plain words, once. This checks duplicate fixes and internal-only wording even while the candidate is unreleased. It uses the recorded publication data; no registry query is needed for this per-change check.

After publishing, finalize that release's heading and record npm's actual version with `node docs/tools/release-history.mjs --record`, then start a `## <next version> (unreleased)` section in [the release notes](docs/user/src/setup/release-notes.md), with a `### Bugs fixed since <last published version>` heading. Repository release pins follow the compiler manifest. Website builds use npm latest, its published platforms and its runtime's Effect pin; an explicit release-version override supports rehearsals.

## Style

Follow the surrounding code and each package's configuration. Format Go with gofmt. Keep TypeScript and VibeLang examples consistent with nearby files, and don't reformat unrelated code. Tests assert behavior, including rejected programs and their diagnostics. Never put credentials or private user content in fixtures, logs or issues.

CONTRIBUTING.md, MAINTAINERS.md and both AGENTS.md files come from `.smithers/flows/docs/project.ts`, except the starter's Essentials, which come from `docs/user/llms-essentials.md`. Edit the source, then run `bun run docs:generate` in `.smithers/`.

## First contributions

Start with [good first issues](https://github.com/smithersai/vibelang/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) or [documentation](https://github.com/smithersai/vibelang/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3Adocumentation). A reduced reproduction of a reported bug or a correction to a guide is a full contribution. Ask on the issue before you start a large change.

## Questions and security

Ask with the [question form](https://github.com/smithersai/vibelang/issues/new?template=question.yml). Report a vulnerability privately, never in an issue: see [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).
